ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a rectangle with a zig-zag line whose vertices alternate between the left and right sides. Starting at the upper-left corner, one segment goes down slightly to the right side and is marked as making 10° with the top horizontal side. The next segment goes back toward the left side, and the angle between these two upper zig-zag segments is marked 14°. Farther down, another pair of zig-zag segments near the right side has angle 33° between them. The bottom-left-to-right segment makes 26° with the bottom horizontal side. The required angle φ is at the left-side middle vertex between the two central zig-zag segments. Reasoning: Since the top and bottom sides of the rectangle are parallel, use the rightward horizontal direction as 0°. The upper segment from the upper-left corner to the right side is 10° below horizontal, so its direction is -10°. The next segment from the left middle point to that same right-side point is 14° above that upper segment, so its direction is -10° + 14° = 4°. The lower segment from the bottom-left corner to the right side makes 26° above horizontal, so its direction is +26°. The central descending segment is 33° below that lower rising segment, so its direction is 26° - 33° = -7°. Therefore angle φ between the central upper segment of direction 4° and the central lower segment of direction -7° is 4° - (-7°) = 11°.

Read that AB makes 10° below the top horizontal side, the angle between AB and CB is 14°, the angle between CD and ED is 33°, and ED makes 26° above the bottom horizontal side. Since the top and bottom of the rectangle are parallel, take the rightward horizontal direction as 0°. Then AB has direction -10°. Because CB lies 14° from AB on the other side of the horizontal, CB has direction 14° - 10° = 4° above horizontal. Also ED has direction +26°, and since CD is 33° below ED, CD has direction 26° - 33° = -7°. Therefore the desired angle at C between CB and CD is 4° - (-7°) = 11°.

method.method_draft: Use a signed-turn or “walking along the zig-zag” method. From the image, traverse the broken line from the upper-left corner to the lower-left corner: first to the upper-right side point, then back to the left side point containing φ, then to the right side point, then to the lower-left corner. Also compare the starting direction with the top side going left-to-right and the ending direction with the bottom side going right-to-left. The top and bottom sides of the rectangle are parallel, so the net direction change from top-east to bottom-west is 180°. Assign clockwise turns negative and counterclockwise turns positive. The successive signed turns are: -10° from the top side to the first segment; -(180° - 14°) at the first right-side kink; +(180° - φ) at the left-side kink; -(180° - 33°) at the second right-side kink; and -26° from the final slanted segment to the bottom side directed right-to-left. Set their sum equal to -180°: -10 - 166 + (180 - φ) - 147 - 26 = -180. Solving gives φ = 11°.
